title: Plasma concentration profiles of ketamine and norketamine after administration of various ketamine preparations to healthy Japanese volunteers

claims.statement: In healthy volunteers given single analgesic amounts in crossover laboratory studies, how much of a ketamine dose reaches the bloodstream depends on the route. Measured against an intravenous dose in the same people, an intramuscular injection gave 93% (0.930, SE 0.026) and a swallowed solution 16.6% (0.166, SE 0.028), each the mean of four people, with a second calculation on all six people giving 19.5% (0.195, SE 0.028) for the swallowed solution (Clements et al., 1982). A later study of three men found 18.3% (SD 4.7) and 17.6% (SD 3.8), for the two mirror-image forms, after a swallowed tablet (Yanagihara et al., 2003), so the oral figure has been found twice by different groups; the intramuscular figure has not been measured again in the sources read here. Blood levels rose fast after the intramuscular injection (peak 243 ng/mL, SE 49, at 22 minutes, SE 4; ketamine present in under 4 minutes; peaks between 100 and 425 ng/mL across people) and stayed low after the swallowed solution (peak 44 ng/mL, SE 10, range 15 to 80, at 30 minutes, SE 5). The 1982 abstract says the oral loss was a failure to absorb, while its own discussion argues that absorption from the gut was complete and the drug was broken down in the liver before reaching the circulation; the metabolite figures in the same paper support the discussion. Both headline figures rest on four people, the intravenous reference is described in a separate five-person study without saying who provided it, and no confidence interval appears anywhere in either paper.
claims.magnitude: Clements et al. (1982): intramuscular Farea 0.930 (SE 0.026, n=4 printed values 0.965, 0.923, 0.972, 0.859); oral Farea 0.166 (SE 0.028, n=4: 0.145, 0.163, 0.112, 0.245) and 0.195 (SE 0.028) from Eq. 2 across 6 people; intramuscular Cmax 243 ng/mL (SE 49) at tmax 22 min (SE 4); oral Cmax 44 ng/mL (SE 10) at 30 min (SE 5). Yanagihara et al. (2003), swallowed tablet in 3 men: bioavailability 18.3% (SD 4.7) for the (R)- and 17.6% (SD 3.8) for the (S)-enantiomer; Cmax 42.6 (SD 13.3) and 40.4 (SD 14.2) ng/mL at 33.3 (SD 15.3) and 30.0 (SD 30.0) min.

claims.statement: In three healthy Japanese men who received five racemic ketamine preparations at least a week apart, measured against the same men's intravenous curves, about 32% of a sublingual tablet reached the bloodstream (32.2%, SD 8.2, and 32.1%, SD 7.2 for the two mirror-image forms), about 29 to 31% of a suppository (28.9%, SD 18.9, and 30.8%, SD 30.6) and about 44 to 46% of a nasal spray (43.8%, SD 11.4, and 46.4%, SD 12.9), the highest figure of the preparations tested (Yanagihara et al., 2003). Peak levels were between 29.3 and 61.6 ng/mL at about 17 to 40 minutes, and the metabolite norketamine was formed least after the nasal spray (area 115.9 and 100.7 ng·h/mL against 533.8 and 494.9 after the swallowed tablet). Each figure is the mean of three men. Two of the conditions did not deliver what their names say: the men swallowed the sublingual tablets with saliva, so that condition was partly gastrointestinal, and not all of them had a bowel preparation before the suppository, which the authors give as the reason the rectal values varied so much that the spread is about the size of the figure itself. The study was open, the order of the five sessions is not described, no test statistic is printed, no elimination half-life is given for any of these preparations, and the two times to peak printed for the nasal spray cannot be means of three measurements taken at the sampling times the paper lists. A 2016 review nonetheless carries the rectal (about 30%) and nasal (about 45%) figures forward, second-hand and without their sample size.
claims.magnitude: Bioavailability, (R)- then (S)-enantiomer: sublingual tablet 32.2% (SD 8.2) and 32.1% (SD 7.2); suppository 28.9% (SD 18.9) and 30.8% (SD 30.6); nasal spray 43.8% (SD 11.4) and 46.4% (SD 12.9); swallowed tablet 18.3% (SD 4.7) and 17.6% (SD 3.8) in the same men. Peaks 61.6 (SD 21.3) and 56.9 (SD 22.8) ng/mL at 40.0 and 36.7 min sublingual, 42.8 (SD 31.1) and 38.8 (SD 30.2) at 23.3 min rectal, 29.4 (SD 16.5) and 29.3 (SD 13.8) at 22.5 and 17.5 min nasal. Norketamine area to 8 hours 115.9 and 100.7 ng·h/mL nasal against 533.8 and 494.9 after the swallowed tablet. n = 3 for every figure.

claims.statement: In 10 healthy volunteers who received, a month apart and in counterbalanced order, a placebo scan, (S)-ketamine and an equimolar amount of (R)-ketamine, the two mirror-image forms did different things. (S)-ketamine produced a short-lived psychosis-like state: depersonalisation and derealisation, visual disturbances from pseudohallucinations to complex hallucinations, thought disorder and apathy, with heightened feelings or euphoria reported by 30%, indifference by 30% and heightened anxiety by 40%, alongside higher scores for deactivation, introversion, emotional irritability and anxiety on a mood scale. The same people on (R)-ketamine reported no psychotic symptoms but a state of relaxation, with only trend-level changes on the scales. Every one of the 10 scored higher under (S)- than under (R)-ketamine on both global scales (altered-states score 37.0, SD 12.6, against 15.6, SD 8.6; ego-pathology score 24.6, SD 11.8, against 1.3, SD 1.6). The brain scans went in opposite directions: (S)-ketamine raised glucose metabolism across most regions, while (R)-ketamine tended to lower it, significantly in the temporomedial cortex on both sides (−13.4%) and the left insula (−14%). Blood levels were similar in the two conditions (mean 379 ng/mL, SD 71, against 389, SD 74) (Vollenweider et al., 1997a). Three things limit this. The blind did not hold: every participant recognised the (R)-ketamine condition as a drug effect, and all had had an (S)-ketamine session beforehand. The two forms were not compared with the racemic mixture in these same people, and the paper's description of the (S) condition as 60% of the racemic amount used earlier does not match the infusion rates printed in the two papers, so its conclusion that (S)-ketamine is the predominant psychotomimetic part of racemic ketamine goes beyond what was measured here. And a separate three-person study found no significant difference between the forms in how the body handles them, which with three people and no test statistic says very little (Yanagihara et al., 2003). A 2016 review reports, second-hand, that S-ketamine has about four times the affinity of R-ketamine for the NMDA receptor and has been postulated to be about four times as potent as R-ketamine and twice as potent as the racemate, that R-ketamine slows the elimination of S-ketamine (clearance 26.3 mL/kg/min for S-ketamine alone against 18.5 for the S-form inside the racemate in ten healthy men), and that the two forms differ in reported side effects.
claims.magnitude: Vollenweider et al. (1997a), n=10, within-person: altered-states global score 37.0 (SD 12.6) under (S)-ketamine against 15.6 (SD 8.6) under (R)-ketamine; ego-pathology global score 24.6 (SD 11.8) against 1.3 (SD 1.6); higher under (S) in all 10 participants (editors' calculation of the within-person difference: 22.6 points, SD 6.3, and 23.3 points, SD 10.9; exact two-sided sign test p = 0.002). Emotional reactions under (S): euphoria or heightened feelings 30%, indifference 30%, heightened anxiety 40%. (R)-ketamine: no psychotic symptoms; oceanic boundlessness p<0.06, well-being p<0.09, emotional irritation p<0.08. Glucose metabolism under (R): whole brain −9.8% (p<0.07, not significant), temporomedial cortex −13.4% bilaterally and left insula −14% (p<0.05). Blood levels 269 to 523 ng/mL (mean 379, SD 71) under (S) and 280 to 508 (mean 389, SD 74) under (R).

claims.statement: After a single intravenous amount in healthy volunteers, blood ketamine falls in two phases, fast at first and then over a few hours. In 1982 the terminal half-life was 186 minutes (standard error 10 in the text and 8 in the table) and total clearance 19.1 mL/min/kg; the half-life after an intramuscular injection, 155 minutes (SE 12), and after a swallowed solution, 174 minutes (SE 50), did not differ significantly from it (Clements et al., 1982). In three men in 2003 the terminal half-life after an intravenous injection was 126.8 minutes (SD 47.4) for the (R)- and 117.3 minutes (SD 47.9) for the (S)-form, with clearance 1.1 and 1.2 L/h/kg, and no half-life is printed for any of that study's other preparations (Yanagihara et al., 2003). A 2016 review gives, second-hand, a distribution half-life of 2 to 4 minutes and an elimination half-life of 2 to 4 hours, with 4 to 7 hours for S-ketamine. The body turns ketamine into norketamine: the review reports that about 80% is converted, that norketamine appears in plasma 2 to 3 minutes after an intravenous injection and peaks at 30 to 60 minutes, and that recent work indicates norketamine is itself broken down quickly and may not be the main substance circulating. Norketamine was measurable after every route in 1982, with peaks of 40 ng/mL (SE 6) after the intravenous, 92 (SE 10) after the intramuscular and 200 (SE 44) after the oral condition, while the dose-corrected areas (35.4, 31.3 and 36.7) were similar, which the authors read as showing that a swallowed dose is absorbed and then broken down in the liver before reaching the circulation. How long ketamine lasts after being swallowed, taken under the tongue, given rectally or sprayed into the nose is not reported in either study.
claims.magnitude: Clements et al. (1982): intravenous terminal half-life 186 min (SE 10 in the Results, SE 8 in Table II), clearance 19.1 mL/min/kg (SE 1.1); intramuscular 155 min (SE 12) and 23.2 mL/min/kg (SE 2.7); oral 174 min (SE 50). Norketamine peaks 40 (SE 6), 92 (SE 10) and 200 ng/mL (SE 44) at 63, 78 and 60 min, dose-corrected areas 35.4 (3.8), 31.3 (3.8) and 36.7 (3.9), described as not significantly different. Yanagihara et al. (2003), intravenous, n=3: 126.8 min (SD 47.4) for (R)- and 117.3 (SD 47.9) for (S)-ketamine; area 138.0 (15.6) and 126.3 (15.1) ng·h/mL; clearance 1.1 (0.2) and 1.2 (0.1) L/h/kg; steady-state volume of distribution 2.5 L/kg. Peltoniemi et al. (2016), second-hand: distribution half-life 2–4 min, elimination 2–4 h (S-ketamine 4–7 h), about 80% converted to norketamine.
